labelChirho: seal, signet mark of authentication or closure
descriptionChirho: A device or its impression used to authenticate, secure, or mark ownership; used both of literal seals (as on the seven seals of Revelation's scroll, or the seal on Christ's tomb) and of metaphorical marks of divine ownership and authentication (Rom 4:11 circumcision as a seal of righteousness; 1 Cor 9:2 believers as a seal of apostleship; 2 Tim 2:19 God's firm foundation bearing a seal). Singular and plural forms represent the same referent class. Spanish 'sello/sellos' (stamp/stamps); Hindi 'मुहर/मुहरें' (seal/seals) from Persian 'muhr'; Arabic 'خَتْم/أختام' (seal/seals) from the root kh-t-m (to seal, conclude); Korean '인' (印, seal/stamp) uses the Sino-Korean character for official stamp; Swahili 'muhuri/mihuri' (seal/seals) is a Bantu-Arabic loan from the same Semitic root as Hindi 'muhr'.
